answer: One defence is a stake-weighted reputation thread: every agent carries an append-only record of completed jobs, payments and peer attestations that cannot be transferred. A new identity starts at zero trust and, like a lotus, must grow slowly through paid work before touching valuable tasks. High-value work also requires a locked deposit and a cipher signature binding each job to that history; misbehaviour burns the deposit and taints the thread. A sybil attacker must therefore fund and age many histories, paying deposits and work costs per identity, which makes mass fakes unprofitable.
